title: Inertia and internal energy: response at λ = 0 and averaged response

key_results.statement: Adding a uniform cost gradient with force $F$ to any diagonal $t_{hh}$ changes $a(0)$ by $\mu F$ with $\mu$ of (20.10) of 03-ilang-space/20-cost-and-mass, for every product start, including starts with zero amplitudes.

For places $(x,a)$: $L_{hh'}(0)=2\operatorname{Re}[(\phi_x)_a^*\langle a\vert T_{xx'}\vert a'\rangle(\phi_{x'})_{a'}]$ and, summed over internal labels, $L_{xx'}(0)=2\operatorname{Re}\langle\phi_x\vert T_{xx'}\vert\phi_{x'}\rangle$.
$\mu=-\sum_{\{x,x'\},x\neq x'}L_{xx'}(0)\,\Delta_{xx'}\,g(\Delta_{xx'},\cdot)$; edges between places with the same $x$ do not contribute.
Decoupled body with start $\phi_X\otimes\eta$: $\mu=-\sum_{\{x,x'\}}2\operatorname{Re}[t_{xx'}\phi_X(x)^*\phi_X(x')]\Delta_{xx'}g(\Delta_{xx'},\cdot)$, independent of $\eta$ and of the $T_{xx}$.
Rest cost of clock level $k$ in Model D: $M_k=m+d_k=m+2\pi k/(N\lambda_0)$, eigenvector $\lvert1\rangle$ at $p=0$; branch gap $2M_k$, curvature $\omega_k''(0)=\tau^2/M_k$.

Model D, start $\phi_X\otimes\lvert1\rangle\otimes\lvert f_k\rangle$: $L_{hh'}(0)=-\frac{2\pi}{N^2\lambda_0}\lvert\phi_X(x)\rvert^2\frac{\sin((2k+1)\pi n/N)}{\sin(\pi n/N)}$ on the edges between $(x,1,a)$ and $(x,1,a')$, $n=a-a'$, and $L_{hh'}(0)=0$ on all other edges.
Model D, start $\phi_X\otimes\lvert1\rangle\otimes\lvert f_k\rangle$: the inverse inertia (20.10) is $\mu=0$ for every $\phi_X$, $k$, $N$, $\tau$, $m$, $\kappa$.
Model D, start concentrated at $p_0=0$ in the positive branch of level $k$, weak records, first order in $F$: $a(\lambda)=\frac{2\tau^2}{M_k}\sin^2(M_k\lambda)\,\kappa^2 g(e,F)\,e$.

Average over $[\lambda_1,\lambda_1+\Lambda]$: $\bar a=\frac{\tau^2}{M_k}\kappa^2 g(e,F)\,e\,[1+O(1/(M_k\Lambda))]$, valid for $1/(2M_k)\ll\Lambda$ and $\mathcal F_{\max}(\lambda_1+\Lambda)\ll\min(1,M_k/\tau)$.
Averaged inverse inertia of Model D: $\mu_{\rm av}(k)=\frac{\tau^2}{m+d_k}\kappa^2\,e\,g(e,\cdot)$.
$M_k\,\mu_{\rm av}(k)=\tau^2\kappa^2 e\,g(e,\cdot)$ for every level: the scalar inertia $M_k/\tau^2$ is the rest cost over $\tau^2$, and the clock cost $d_k$ adds to it like the rest term $m$.

Decoupled chain body with hopping $t$ and any clock term: $\mu_{\rm av}=\mu=\kappa^2\langle\phi_X\vert\omega''(\hat p)\vert\phi_X\rangle\,e\,g(e,\cdot)$ with $\omega(p)=te^{-ip}+t^*e^{ip}$, independent of the clock level.
Comparison: for Model D $\mu=0\neq\mu_{\rm av}(k)$; for the decoupled body $\mu=\mu_{\rm av}$, because its velocity commutes with $C_b$, while in Model D the velocity connects the two branches.

open_issues: A ticking clock (superposition of levels) is not treated; by level conservation its averaged response is the level-weighted mean of (6.15), and whether this is the inertia of one body is open.
Beyond fixed λ, Model D uses the stated standard adiabatic branch response and the concentration limit; for wide packets the average ⟨ω_k''⟩ is expected but not derived.
Second order in κ (record decoherence, κ²σ_X²) and in F (drift beyond the quadratic region, Bloch oscillation, branch transitions) is not treated.
The meaning of τ as a maximal speed and of M_k/τ² belongs to criteria 4 and 6 and is outside this package (M1, M3).

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions of (6.9), (6.13), (6.15), and the limit τ → 0 (no motion)
a(0) = 0 for every F from the equations of motion (6.12), independently of μ = 0 from (20.10) in (6.10)
Cost sum rule: site plus edge costs of D at one point give d_k |φ_X(x)|²
